chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Uthman ibn Isa from Khalid ibn Najih from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:
The Earth will never be void of four believers; they may be more numerous, but they will never be fewer than four. This is because a tent cannot stand except with four ropes and a central pillar.
ai.seo_question: Why does the Earth need at least four believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs the architectural analogy of a tent (fustat) requiring four ropes and a central pillar to illustrate the concept of *Hujjah* (Proof), asserting that the Earth is never devoid of four specific groups of believers who maintain cosmic order. This tradition highlights the Shia belief in the continuous presence of divine guidance through the Ahl al-Bayt and the broader community of faithful, ensuring the stability of the world until the Day of Resurrection.
